function: Refines a preliminary SOMP near-field channel estimate with a conditional generative diffusion model (NM-GDM) for uplink XL-MIMO channel estimation (p. 2, 4-5).
system: Uplink XL-MIMO OFDM: BS with 256-antenna ULA and 16 RF chains (hybrid), 16 single-antenna users, 28 GHz, 100 MHz, 256 subcarriers; no RIS (p. 3, 10).
method: Conditional denoising diffusion model (GDM) and non-Markovian NM-GDM, UNet-like with ResNet and attention blocks, supervised by ELBO noise-prediction loss; conditioned on SOMP estimate; trained offline (p. 5-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: spherical-wavefront joint angle-distance channel (L=6 paths) generated following [15]; 70,000 pairs of SOMP estimate and true channel, split 5:1:1; no public data (p. 3, 10).
test_conditions: Training data from the Table I setup (N=256); tests sweep SNR, pilots, BS antennas and distance in NF and FF; retraining per sweep not stated (p. 10-14).
baselines: Learned: CNN-based L-DAMP. Non-learned: polar-domain SOMP (first stage), SIGW, SW-OMP, SS-SIGW-OLS, LS, genie-aided LS bound; GDM versus NM-GDM sampling comparison (p. 13).
metrics: NMSE (dB) versus SNR, pilot length, BS antennas, distance and sampling steps; convergence loss; GFLOPs and parameters (p. 11-14).
complexity: 7.82 GFLOPs and 11.82 million parameters for chosen NM-GDM; first stage O(L Q NRF S K); NM-GDM about 10 times faster sampling than GDM (p. 11-13).
q1_support: p. 10: "H is generated following the method in [15]"; custom spherical-wavefront angle-distance model with L = 6 paths (Table I, p. 10); no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 13: "we vary the number of BS antennas and the distance to strengthen or weaken their corresponding NF effects"; but the data come from the single setup of Table I (N = 256, p. 10) and the paper never states that one trained model is tested at another N, pilot length or distance range without retraining.
q3_support: p. 13: "we compare the proposed NM-GDM with the state-of-art algorithms, including the CNN-based L-DAMP [33], the polar-domain SOMP [15] and SIGW algorithms [15]"; SW-OMP, SS-SIGW-OLS and LS follow, all compared on NMSE (Figs. 8-11).
q4_support: p. 12: "resulting in 7.82 GFLOPs and 11.82 million parameters"; the first stage is O(L Q NRF S K) (p. 11) and NM-GDM samples about 10 times faster than GDM (p. 13).
q5_support: p. 10: "The training, validation, and testing sets are divided in a 5 : 1 : 1 ratio"; the 70,000 channel pairs are simulated (p. 10) and no code or data link, DOI or public dataset is given.
notes: Included as area 2: the diffusion model refines a SOMP channel estimate. Preprint arXiv 2505.06900v1 (p. 1). The output of scripts/pdf_text.py for this file shifts and truncates pages 11-15 because of stray form feeds from figure fonts; pages cited here are the real PDF pages, read from page images and a per-page extraction. q2 is 0 because train and test conditions are not separated explicitly; the reviewer may check Figs. 8-11 and the text of p. 13, where N, pilot length and distance are varied.
